contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Mehmed II was Ottoman sultan and conqueror of Constantinople, the ruler whose 1453 victory ended the Byzantine Empire and made the city an Ottoman capital. His reign connected artillery warfare, imperial ideology, urban rebuilding, legal authority, and Mediterranean diplomacy.

Born in Edirne in 1432, Mehmed ruled twice and returned to the throne with a program of expansion. He died near Gebze in 1481, leaving an empire that had become a major European and Near Eastern power and a legacy as both conqueror and imperial founder.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Mehmed was born in 1432 at Edirne, then a major Ottoman center in Europe. He was the son of Murad II and grew up in a court shaped by warfare in the Balkans, Islamic learning, dynastic politics, and the frontier world between the Ottoman Empire and Christian powers.

He first became sultan as a youth in 1444, but political and military pressure brought Murad II back to power. That early interruption helped shape Mehmed’s later determination to command authority directly.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Mehmed II combined intellectual curiosity with overwhelming imperial ambition, and the sources — Ottoman, Greek, and Italian — present a ruler who was as fascinated by knowledge as by conquest. He read history, was drawn to the legacy of Rome and Alexander, commissioned the Italian painter Gentile Bellini to portray him, and styled himself heir to the Roman imperial tradition after taking Constantinople in 1453. That self-image as a universal emperor shaped his entire reign.

He was also ruthless and calculating to a degree that unsettled even his own court. He institutionalised fratricide for the sake of dynastic stability, drove his armies and engineers to extraordinary feats at the siege of Constantinople, and pursued relentless campaigns in the Balkans and Anatolia. Greek and Italian writers who feared him emphasised cruelty; Ottoman writers emphasised vision and justice. The truth the record supports is a ruler of cold strategic patience capable of sudden, decisive violence.

His personality mattered directly to history: the fall of Constantinople owed much to his refusal to abandon a difficult siege, and his fusion of scholarly ambition with conquest set the cultural tone of the empire he transformed. He is best understood not as a simple tyrant but as a calculating, intellectually restless empire-builder.

contentSections.title: As sultan of the Ottoman Empire
paragraphs: Mehmed returned to the throne in 1451 and prepared carefully for the siege of Constantinople. He built Rumeli Hisari, assembled artillery, controlled the Bosporus, and pressed the Ottoman claim to imperial succession.

The Fall of Constantinople in 1453 made him famous as Mehmed the Conqueror. He rebuilt the city, drew communities into it, patronized learning and art, and expanded Ottoman authority through campaigns in the Balkans and Anatolia.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Died near Gebze in 1481 while on campaign; the precise illness and campaign objective remain debated.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: Mehmed is remembered above all for conquering Constantinople and transforming it into an Ottoman capital. In Ottoman memory he became Fatih, the Conqueror; in Byzantine and European memory he marked the end of an empire.
His legacy belongs to both medieval and early modern history: he ended one Roman imperial tradition while claiming and remaking another through Ottoman power.

timeline.title: Born
timeline.description: Mehmed was born at Edirne, an Ottoman capital in Europe, into the dynasty that was pressing against Byzantine Constantinople and the Balkans.

timeline.description: Briefly takes the Ottoman throne as a youth.

timeline.title: Returns to the throne
timeline.description: Becomes sultan again after Murad II's death.

timeline.title: Builds Rumeli Hisari
timeline.description: Constructs a fortress on the Bosporus to pressure Constantinople.

timeline.title: Conquers Constantinople
timeline.description: Ends the Byzantine Empire and makes the city an Ottoman capital.

timeline.title: Captures Trebizond
timeline.description: Ends the last major Byzantine successor state.
